key_insight: A physics-guided neural differential equation reduced-order model can capture multi-mode aeroelastic oscillations and transonic buffet dynamics using a single CFD training simulation.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a much cheaper way to predict aeroelastic stability, frequency lock-in, and limit-cycle amplitudes for flutter/buffet problems than repeated full-order CFD analysis.
method: Nonlinear fluid oscillator + finite-memory multi-input Volterra series
Neural-network correction to represent residual unmodeled dynamics
Generalized to multiple structural modes and coupled to structural equations of motion
evidence_signal: The ROM was identified from one prescribed-motion CFD case with simultaneous multi-mode excitation and then validated on ONERA OAT15A buffet predictions against full-order reference solutions.
watch_item: Performance may depend on having a representative excitation case and careful handling of regime changes when extrapolating beyond the training motion or flow conditions.
paper_title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations for Oscillatory Flows in Aeroelasticity with Application to Transonic Buffet
